title: Presence and count weights gave near-spatial thermal responses at 62 Finnish moth sites
abstract: We tested whether abundance weights explain the near-spatial thermal response reported for Finnish moths. We used 1,243 annual samples at 62 sites in 1993-2022, species counts, European thermal scores and continuous GHCN-CAMS air temperature. Presence and count indices rose by 0.141 and 0.140 C per decade. Their spatial slopes were 0.219 and 0.215 C/C. Relative to each spatial warming expectation, their trend ratios were 1.12 (95% spatial-block interval 0.89-1.44) and 1.13 (0.87-1.52). The paired difference was -0.012 (-0.251 to 0.226). Expected presence at a fixed catch of 1,000 individuals gave a ratio of 0.994 at 53 matched sites. Thus removal of abundance weights did not reveal weak transfer in this release. This limits an abundance-only explanation of the Finnish contrast. The data overlap prior Finnish studies. Detected species exchange is not demographic colonisation or extinction. Source selection, effort, detectability, common year shocks and spatial habitat gradients limit causal inference. We provide code, aggregate results, source hashes and a reproducible external-data recipe.

display.caption: Matched records under count, square-root and presence weights. Bars show 95% spatial-block intervals. Dashed line shows the spatial warming expectation. Ratios are descriptive, not causal warming fractions.
